title: TRU starring Jesse Tyler Ferguson #jessetylerferguson #trumancapote #...
transcript: In this immersive production starring Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Truman Capote is drinking alone at Christmastime, shuffling around his apartment to tell us why. Having recently published an excerpt from a novel of his, he's on the outs with his wealthy friends who are not-so-secretly the novel’s subject. We get the backstory for this situation but we also get broader musings on life, art, and wealth, for example. Jesse Tyler Ferguson's performance feels grounded and not overly imitative, though for a character study, the piece doesn't give him all that much room to develop or show a lot of range. What we get out of the 90 minutes isn't much more than what we get out of the first 60 or so. Perhaps this is all just a result of the play being adapted from the words and works of Truman Capote himself, but I felt like we were getting a curated version of him, as opposed to a more unguarded version that would have better suited such an intimate production, even if it meant taking more character liberties. In general, I'm not sure the direction of this production makes the case for its immersiveness — the audience isn't really folded in or utilized in any notable way. Of course, plenty of folks appreciate the close proximity to Jesse Tyler Ferguson, as evident by the ticket sales, but that factor alone doesn't quite sustain a 90 minute monodrama. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: Creator describes seeing the immersive production starring Jesse Tyler Ferguson as Truman Capote, providing detailed plot summary and analysis
reasoning: The reviewer presents a balanced critique with both appreciation (grounded performance, interesting subject) and significant reservations (limited character development, questionable use of immersive format). No clear recommendation emerges.
